5.text: Their eyes are straight, and frequently as large as those of Caucasians,

6.text: and plica occurs but rarely among them; and their hair, as well as that of

7.text: the Koryak, is often wavy or even curly, while the Kamchadal always have

8.text: straight hair. Several Reindeer Chukchee that I met in various parts of their

9.text: territory had the surname “curly” (kaˊmčɪ) because of their very curly hair;

11.text: in Pacific villages even looked woolly. This effect was produced because the

12.text: hair was coarse and thick, and at the same time formed tight curls.

13.text: In the interior and on the Arctic coast the color of the hair is black,

14.text: but on the Pacific coast about fifteen per cent of the people have dark-brown

15.text: or even light-brown hair. The growth of hair on the face is scanty, but

16.text: beards are more frequently seen than among the Lamut or the Yakut.

17.text: Accordingly, while the Lamut are very careful to pull out the beard-hair with

18.text: tweezers, the Chukchee frequently allow their beards to grow, and are even

19.text: proud of them. With the Reindeer people a mustache (or, rather, the appear-

20.text: ance of a black down on the upper lip) is considered the crowning feature of

21.text: full growth, the warrant of independence. The eyebrows are often thick and

22.text: bushy, especially among old men. The growth of hair on the body is scanty.

23.text: Thick eyebrows, long thick braids, and hairy pubes are counted as marks of

24.note: Footnote reference, raised superscript digit confirmed at 4x (keying_spec.md §2.10); keyed as U+00B9, never ASCII 1.

25.text: The color of the face is bronze, with intermediate tints varying from

26.text: brick-red to blood-red. The ideal of beauty in both sexes requires that the

27.text: face be “as red as blood, burning like fire.” The color of the skin of the

28.text: body is generally scarcely distinguishable from that of Caucasians. There are,

29.text: however, numerous cases of brown or even dark-brown skin, more frequently

30.text: among the Maritime Chukchee. The latter even consider the brownish com-

31.text: plexion to be the handsomest. The breasts of women who are with child

32.text: frequently assume a dark-brown color over the whole surface.

33.text: One of the marks of superiority is the ability to eat quickly. “When

34.text: the young men eat quickly, the old men look on with pleasure,” says the

35.text: proverb. Accordingly the Reindeer Chukchee have adopted a peculiarly fierce

36.text: and hasty method of eating, accompanied by sounds reminding one of the

37.text: snarling of a hungry dog. One of the young herdsmen whom I saw on the

38.text: Anui River acquired so much skill in this respect, that he could strip a whole

39.text: joint of its flesh by taking hold of it with his teeth and pulling off first one

40.text: side, then the other, — “like a wolf,” his companions remarked admiringly.
